To the Editor:
Re “
British Premier Urges Military to Spend More to Fight ISIS
” (news article, July 13):
While you report that Prime Minister David Cameron wants more of Britain’s “military budget to be spent on tackling Islamic extremism, citing special forces, spy planes and drones as probable priorities,” his call runs up against a major stumbling block.
In recent years of defense cuts, so much of that budget is still spent on expensive, quasi-Cold War items like aircraft carriers and, in particular, Trident nuclear submarines that more flexible, rapid-response forces have been something of an afterthought.
PHILIP G. CERNY
York, England
The writer is professor emeritus of politics and global affairs at Rutgers University and the University of Manchester.

Helen Roosevelt beneath family portraits in her home on East 61st Street. The former board member of the Roosevelt Hospital is dismayed that Mount Sinai has formally removed the name of the Roosevelt family from the hospital they founded.
The Mount Sinai Health System renamed the Manhattan hospital in November.
